held.title: The Fervor
held.author: Alma Katsu
held.reason: Supernatural CONFIRMED (Iglesias, Locus: 'their lives are full of yokai - apparitions and supernatural entities - and the jorogumo, a yokai that appears in the story as a spider demon') in 1940s Minidoka internment camp. war-gothic is the shape ('war's unresolved dead and accumulated violence return to haunt') but its def gates the contemporary world, and this is 1940s historical; monsters-in-gaslight is 19th-century. A genuine call for the curator's ear, no lean.

held.title: The Honeys
held.author: Ryan La Sala
held.reason: Speculative real but nature unquoted: Kirkus - 'Events soon take strange and fantastic twists as Mars realizes that time and people seem to vanish' around the Honeys' camp apiary; Reactor's Brown calls it 'true horror... not dark fantasy'. cursed-towns names camps explicitly (bend: the menace may be the Honeys themselves, not the ground). A genuine call for the curator's ear, no lean.

held.title: The Kindred
held.author: Alechia Dow
held.reason: YA space opera whose engine is the implanted Kindred pairing chip and the class divide between a dirt-poor planet and royalty, Ilori invaders in the background (Brown, Locus). No fitting leaf: new-space-opera partitions by adventure, politics, theology and shipboard drama, none of which matches; near-trunk stall held for the curator ruling.

held.title: The Midnight Timetable
held.author: Bora Chung
held.reason: A 'novel in ghost stories': an institute cataloguing supernatural objects, linked tales whose haunted items recur, dread mosaic (Kirkus). No leaf fits: ghost-stories children want a single bound revenant, mediums or lesson-carrying dead; residual-haunting is Stone-Tape replay without agent, and these hauntings have agency. Held for the curator's ear.

held.title: The Parliament
held.author: Aimee Pokwatka
held.reason: Small-town library under siege by tens of thousands of homicidal owls, The Birds lineage, contemporary West Virginia (Mondor/Pierce, Locus). No animal-attack/predator leaf exists: cryptid-horror wants a hidden species, beasts-of-marvel is people becoming animals. Near-trunk gap held for the curator's ear.

held.title: The Shadow Sister
held.author: Lily Meade
held.reason: Magic-based final twist and subtle hoodoo confirmed (Locus; author interview), but supernatural mechanism and defining about-ness remain unclear; no clean existing leaf. Curator ear requested.

held.title: The Spice Gate
held.author: Prashanth Srivatsa
held.reason: Caste escape, journey to a hidden ninth kingdom and eventual emancipation (PW, Library Journal, Scroll). Existing Destiny Quest requires marked heir, Revisionist Quest critiques heroic template, political subleaves demand revolt/intrigue machinery; no clean home. Curator ear requested.

standing_rules.name: Absurd Shit rule
standing_rules.source: the curator: "I'm making an 'Absurd Shit'-rule: if it's too absurd to say if it's SF or Fantasy, and it's not even a Fabulation: kill it"
standing_rules.apply: Autonomous, no per-case ask: if a book is too absurd to call SF or Fantasy AND fits no Fabulation node, exclude as not SFF. Log each kill in sweep.log as '-Title (Absurd Shit rule)' and in excluded[] with reason citing the rule.
